nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What has been somewhat lacking in the discussion about gardens and urban birds, according to the paper?
nodes.answer: The discussion has been lacking in topics that address important additional factors beyond just the selection of plant species to attract birds.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Inadequacies in public protected area networks dictates that private land will play an important role in the conservation of biodiversity in the coming decades. Household gar - dens are a key example of private lands that can serve as refuges for biodiversity, with birds as a popular flagship for garden biodiversity. Discussion has focused heavily on the species of plant a resident might select to attract birds to their garden. In this paper, we describe additional and important factors that should form part of this broader conversation on gardens for birds and biodiversity, with a specific aim of drawing attention to species that are at risk of localised extinctions in modern urban landscapes urban adaptors. We present our commentary in two themes: (a) mitigating threats to birds in the urban environ- ment and (b) enhancing the habitat value of the urban environment for a broader range of bird species. We provide a synthesis of the research of recent years that has explored the urban environment and its ability to support birds, but importantly, we extend on this by bringing together topics that have been somewhat lacking in the discussion to date.

nodes.question: What broader issue does the suitability of gardens as bird refuges relate to in Australia?
nodes.answer: The suitability of gardens as bird refuges is connected to a national policy landscape that has not effectively prevented vegetation clearing at a continental scale.

Secondly, many gardens can provide an important source of water (via birdbaths or other water fea- tures) (Cleary et al. 2016; Gibbons et al. 2023), which will be critical in many areas pre- dicted to experience significant drying as a result of anthropogenic climate change (Grose 1141 Biodiversity and Conservation (2025) 34:1139 1154 et al. 2020). Thirdly, gardens can serve as important stepping stones for many birds that move through the landscape between larger patches of intact habitat (Goddard et al. 2017). This final point may be important in the context of areas where local and state government agencies routinely burn these urban-adjacent patches of habitat; the impacts of which are poorly documented for birds (but see Bradshaw et al. 2018). In these scenarios, resident birds may seek out urban and peri-urban gardens in search of refuge during periods of prescribed burning. nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the paper regarding urban gardens and birds?
nodes.answer: The paper emphasizes how urban gardens can support birds, especially urban adaptors, by highlighting factors beyond just plant species selection, including providing food, water, and stepping stones for movement between habitat patches.

nodes.label: Conservation
nodes.question: What role do urban gardens play in supporting Australian bird species, according to the paper?
nodes.answer: Urban gardens can provide reliable food resources, important sources of water, and serve as stepping stones for birds moving through the landscape, especially when larger patches of intact habitat are compromised.
nodes.paragraph: We present our commentary in two themes: (a) mitigating threats to birds in the urban environ- ment and (b) enhancing the habitat value of the urban environment for a broader range of bird species. We provide a synthesis of the research of recent years that has explored the urban environment and its ability to support birds, but importantly, we extend on this by bringing together topics that have been somewhat lacking in the discussion to date. In a new approach to this conversation, this paper brings together key topics that can no longer be considered in isolation if we are to make significant conservation gains in the environ- ments were most Australians now reside. nodes.question: What factors do gardens provide that support bird species in urban environments?
nodes.answer: Gardens often provide reliable food resources, crucial water sources, and serve as stepping stones for birds to navigate between larger patches of intact habitat.

Research also supports the notion that some urban exploiters may themselves pose a barrier to adaptors persisting in urban settings; where noisy miners are consistently found to have a negative influence on the presence of many other less aggressive species (Maron et al. 2013; Davis et al. 2015; Campbell et al. 2022; Humphrey et al. 2023, 2024). With continued growth in greenfield and infill urban development, urban adaptors will likely decline in many urban landscapes (Thomson et al. 2022); the design of which tends to favour urban exploiters. This has been and continues to pose a threat to many spe- cies resulting in increased fragmentation and population declines and is a trend observed beyond the Australian context (Aronson et al. 2014). The ability for urban adaptors to per - sist will strongly depend on the actions and behaviours of urban residents. In this paper we seek to broaden and integrate the discussion on how urban gardens can best support birds beyond plant species selection alone, with an emphasis on accommodat- ing urban adaptors.
